correctness.rationale: Reconstructing the graph from the published overlap definition gives exactly 81 vertices and 237 undirected loop-free edges. The supplied colouring assigns all vertices to three classes of sizes 28, 30 and 23 and the verifier checks every edge is bichromatic. The three vertices 0000, 0001 and 1000 form a triangle, so two colours are impossible. A fresh independent DSATUR-style reconstruction found a valid three-colouring and independently confirmed the same vertex/edge counts and triangle. The standard theorem then implies word-representability.

The later Huang–Kitaev–Pyatkin paper was materially read in full: it explicitly restates that conjecture, recalls that every 3-colourable graph is word-representable, and proves positive results only for restricted induced subgraphs \(S_m(n,k)\), not the full \(S(4,3)\). A current MathDB entry still labels the conjecture open and records no progress. Resultary searches found no prior colouring or positive full-graph statement.

final_claim: The full simplified de Bruijn graph \(S(4,3)\) has chromatic number exactly 3 and is therefore word-representable; this refutes the published conjecture that every \(S(n,k)\) with \(n\ge4\) and \(k\ge3\) is non-word-representable.
